entries.answer: Git is a version control system, so it records the history of a project and lets you see what changed, when and by whom. A commit is one snapshot, and a branch is a movable label pointing at a commit, which is why branching is cheap enough to do per feature. The habit that matters is committing and merging often, because a branch left alone for a month is a conflict nobody wants.
